description: Connect the actual local disposable test app to the FetchSandbox verifier, without installing ngrok or sharing an account token. Local stdio coding agents only; hosted builders use their published app origin. Steps: (1) inspect the real app, its provider clients, existing webhook handler route, signature verification and saved-state read-back; never invent a substitute webhook route or remove signature checks. (2) Start that app on a loopback port and call action=open,port. (3) Call validate_integration with providers and the returned app_base_url; retain session_id. (4) Inspect coverage_policy, propose application checks, prepare/read back fixtures, and configure suite=application_workflow_v1. Register the exact inspected webhook path in application_config.event_destinations, e.g. stripe:/stripe-webhook ONLY if that is the real handler. For Stripe purchase verification, set application_config.event_delivery=provider_lifecycle. FetchSandbox registers this exact tunnel route using the isolated Stripe twin POST /v1/webhook_endpoints, returns registration metadata, and supplies its signing secret through the protected handoff. Drive the real app order/payment entry points and confirm/capture its actual PaymentIntent; do not replace the purchase with synthetic success events. Assert saved order and email effects. Other provider lifecycle registrations remain explicit gaps; existing hosted receipt suites keep their current path. Direct signed-event mode remains for targeted event tests and is not full purchase lifecycle proof. Use provider-native event types/payloads and exact event-ID replay. (5) Use the native protected handoff: call install_test_credentials with session_id/run_id and inspected env_mapping; load its private dotenv file into the disposable app without reading or printing it. Configure temporary provider base URLs; preserve production configuration. The relay credential is internal and never goes to the app. (6) Preflight, execute ONCE, then poll the same session_id/run_id and retrieve its receipt. Independently assert order/state and receipt effects across replay, concurrent/stale/delayed events, invalid signatures and relevant provider failures, response loss and restart. HTTP 200 or connectivity alone is not proof; retain unsupported/unmeasured checks. Compare original buggy and fixed app versions under the same contract. (7) Close the tunnel and clean temporary settings. If local startup/connectivity fails, retain the blocker and use the existing Phalanx prove_fix fallback. This temporary address is verifier-only, not a public website. Direct browser/curl requests deliberately return 404 even when the relay is healthy. Do not treat that 404 as failed connectivity, inspect FetchSandbox internals, expose relay credentials or switch verification paths because of it. After configuration and credential installation, use validate_integration preflight to test actual app connectivity; manage_tunnel status checks only the transport. A disconnect or backend restart ends the lease; do not automatically replay uncertain writes.
name: manage_tunnel
